$comment: Known answers for home-loan eligibility by FOIR (fixed obligations to income ratio). Published worked examples found via web search on 2026-10-09 (direct fetch of the pages is blocked in the build environment). Rounded figures carry a tolerance; the ₹57,61,542 figure is exact to the rupee. Exact behaviour is also checked in tools-core/test/eligibility.test.ts against the present value of an annuity (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mortgage_calculator) and against computeEmi.

cases.name: ₹1 lakh a month, 50% FOIR, no existing EMIs, 8.5%, 20 years
cases.quote: Using an indicative interest rate of 8.5% per annum over a 20-year tenure … 50% … ₹50,000 … ₹57,61,542

cases.name: ₹50,000 a month, 50% FOIR, no existing EMIs, 8.5%, 20 years
cases.quote: quick reference assuming 8.5% interest, 20-year tenure, zero existing EMIs, 50% FOIR … about ₹28.8 lakh for ₹50,000 income

cases.name: ₹80,000 a month, 50% FOIR, no existing EMIs, 8.5%, 20 years
cases.quote: reduces your home loan eligibility from about Rs 46 lakh (no existing EMIs) to about Rs 29 lakh (with Rs 15,000 existing EMI) at 8.5% for 20 years

cases.name: ₹80,000 a month, 50% FOIR, ₹15,000 existing EMIs, 8.5%, 20 years
